options.description: Slice #36. Opt-in per-run toggles that shape how the kernel treats partially-specified programs. Absent is default (backward-compatible with all pre-#36 fixtures).

strict_framing.description: When true, effect / probability queries whose referenced predicates still have A0 framing gaps flip to needs_investigation before numeric evaluation. The F1 DEFINE_VARIABLE channel still fires with the same skeletons so the fill-back loop is unchanged — only the numeric path is gated.

confidence.description: Composite confidence score for the whole input item; not a statistical interval.

evidence.description: Phase 4 / A2: free-text evidence quote(s) supporting this annotation. String for a single source paragraph; list of strings when merged across multiple narrative extractions. Reasoning rules do not read this — it is provenance metadata for downstream rendering / audit only.

annotations.description: Slice A2: provenance / confidence metadata for this edge, e.g. {"source": "llm_proposal"} for a hypothesis edge, {"source": "PubMed:..."} for an evidence-backed edge. Reasoning rules do not read this.

populationName.description: Phase 9 §T9.1: a population identifier. Used to label probability statements with the source population they came from, and to label queries with the target population whose effect is wanted. Must be a valid identifier (snake_case recommended).

selectionNodeStatement.description: Phase 9 §T9.1. A selection node in a Bareinboim-Pearl selection diagram. Declares that the variable named in ``affects`` has a different distribution between the source and target populations — the canonical reason transport identification needs adjustment. Reasoning rules read it; verifier audits S-admissibility against it.

id.description: Stable identifier for this S node (e.g. ``S_age``). Used in derivation steps so the user can trace which S node a transport step references.

affects.description: The atom whose distribution differs across populations. Conceptually there is an arrow S → affects in the selection diagram; this field declares that arrow's head.

annotations.description: Provenance / evidence for the claim that distributions differ (e.g. {"source": "narrative_proposal", "evidence": "源人群均值 42 岁; 目标 28 岁"}). Reasoning does not read this.

bidirectedStatement.description: Phase 2.latent S1. An undirected 'bidirected' edge between two observed atoms, semantically declaring the existence of at least one unobserved common cause (semi-Markov representation). The kind is accepted by the schema but cannot yet be dispatched by the runtime — programs containing bidirectedStatement raise SemanticError until Phase 2.latent S2+ lands m-separation + c-component support. See PHASE_2_LATENT_CHARTER.md.

annotations.description: Provenance / confidence metadata for the bidirected edge. Not consumed by reasoning rules in S1.

target.description: Target atom with the specific value this conditional refers to, e.g. {atom: cancer(X), value: true}.

given.description: Model conditioning set for the target, each entry a groundedAtom at a specific value. In v0.1 this should align with the target's structural parent set, or a subset of it.

value.description: Model-world conditional probability value, not an empirical sample frequency.

population.description: Phase 9 §T9.1: optional source-population label. Probability statements without this field are treated as universal across populations (back-compat).

given.description: Condition set for the structural association query.

target.description: Target atom with the specific value whose probability under intervention is being queried, e.g. {atom: cancer(alice), value: true}.

given.description: Observed condition set applied together with the intervention, each at a specific value.

mediator.description: Phase 6.mediation: when present, the query asks for a mediation decomposition (NDE/NIE/CDE) through this mediator atom rather than a plain total effect. Omitting the field preserves total-effect semantics.

target_population.description: Phase 9 §T9.1: when present, the effect is wanted in this target population, not in the population the data was collected from. Triggers transport identification — requires at least one selectionNodeStatement to be meaningful.

assumptions.description: Iter 131: first-class assumption block parallel to CounterfactualQuery.assumptions. Optional. Currently carries optional `monotonicity` for the iter 119 Manski-Tamer bounds path; promoted from the iter 119 program.extensions['monotonicity'] side-channel hack to a query-level field. Scheduler still falls back to extensions when this is absent for backwards compat.

monotonicity.description: Direction of monotone treatment response (Manski 1997). When set, EffectQuery's bounds layer tightens one side of Manski natural to the observed marginal. Same semantic as CounterfactualQuery.assumptions.monotonicity.

given.description: Observed condition set for the interventional quantity to be identified.

target_population.description: Phase 9 §T9.1: when present, asks whether the interventional quantity is identifiable in this target population (transport identification). Requires at least one selectionNodeStatement.

target.description: Target atom with the specific value whose conditional probability is being queried.

observed.description: Observed factual world assignment, e.g. chose_major=false.

counterfactual_target.description: Counterfactual target event whose probability is being queried.

variableDeclaration.description: Advisory per-predicate framing metadata (slice A0). Declaring a variable opts it into framing_notes: any unset field becomes a gap reported on queries that reference this predicate. Omitting a declaration silences framing for that predicate; nothing here gates reasoning.

domain.description: Enumerated value domain, e.g. [true, false] or ["low","mid","high"]. Used only for framing; the runtime still reads actual domains from observed values.

time_window.description: Natural-language time window the variable refers to, e.g. "12w" or "single exam".

measurement.description: How the variable is measured, e.g. "waist circumference cm" or "self-reported daily minutes".

threshold.description: Cutoff that turns a continuous measurement into this predicate's value, e.g. ">=3cm".

observability.description: Whether the variable is observable / self-reported / latent in this setting.

direction.description: Slice #41. Effect polarity the predicate commits to: e.g. "up" (the predicate fires when the underlying quantity increases), "down", "mixed". Surfaces questions where '影响 X' is ambiguous between raise / lower / fluctuate.

baseline.description: Slice #41. The reference level a change is measured from, e.g. "pre-intervention clinic BP", "school-reported mid-term score". Surfaces questions like '提高数学成绩' where improvement relative to what baseline is not stated.

state_vs_event.description: Slice #41. Whether the predicate describes a habitual / persistent state or a discrete event: "state" vs "event". Surfaces ambiguity between e.g. '跟同事闹矛盾' as a one-off episode versus an ongoing relational state.
